newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO, Russia fix date for more talks.
newsitem.headline: NATO, Russia fix date for more talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana will hold a new round of talks on a pact defining a new post-Cold War relationship on May 6 in Luxembourg, alliance sources said on Monday.

The fifth round of talks to try to reach a deal before the alliance proceeds with its plans to expand eastwards into former communist Europe follows an intensive bout of diplomacy to try to overcome the remaining obstacles. Russia is demanding limits on military activities in any new member states.
President Boris Yeltsin visited Germany last week and said he hoped the landmark NATO-Russia pact would be ready for signing in Paris on May 27.

That would clear the way for at least Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to be invited to join the alliance at a special summit in Madrid in July. The U.S. has reacted coolly to Yeltsin's comments, believing he is trying to coax the alliance into making some last-minute concessions.
Moscow has agreed four-fifths of a new document or "charter" with NATO creating a permanent consultative mechanism and giving Russia a voice in many NATO activities.

Primakov, however, has made demands which would prevent the new states from upgrading their military facilities to bring them in line with alliance requirements -- a demand totally rejected by the West as creating a "second-class" membership.
